litigation.mdlName: In re: Lyft, Inc. Passenger Sexual Assault Litigation
litigation.court: U.S. District Court, Northern District of California

phaseDetail: The November 9 order requires plaintiffs in six named cases to respond by November 23, 2026 about why their cases should remain open after alleged failures to serve timely fact sheets.

settlements.label: No settlement program announced
settlements.detail: No global settlement program or public payout schedule for MDL-3171 was identified in records reviewed October 17, 2026. The MDL is in its first year of pretrial proceedings.
settlements.source: JPML transfer order and October 1, 2026 JPML report
settlements.individualClaims: No official individual payout amounts have been published.

keyDates.label: MDL-3171 created
keyDates.detail: The JPML centralized 17 actions from 10 districts before Judge Rita F. Lin in the Northern District of California. Lyft had opposed centralization.

keyDates.label: 134 pending federal cases
keyDates.detail: Up from 72 on the August 3 JPML report.

keyDates.label: Fact-sheet show-cause responses due
keyDates.detail: The November 9 order required plaintiffs in six named cases to respond by November 23 about alleged failures to serve timely fact sheets. The deadline has passed. The Northern District of California public new-filings index reviewed through November 24 does not publish a dismissal order or another outcome for those six cases, so no case disposition is inferred.
keyDates.appliesTo: Plaintiffs in the six cases named in the November 9 order

updates.summary: The November 23 show-cause response deadline for six case-specific plaintiffs has passed. The Northern District of California public new-filings index reviewed through November 24 does not publish a dismissal order or other outcome for those cases.
The November 9 order requires plaintiffs in six named cases to respond by November 23, 2026 about why their cases should remain open after alleged failures to serve timely fact sheets.
JPML lists 150 pending and 164 historical actions in MDL-3171 on November 2, compared with 134 pending on October 1.
JPML reports 134 pending actions in MDL-3171 on October 1, 2026, up from 106 on September 1; 148 total historical actions are reported separately.
JPML reports 106 pending actions on September 1, 2026, compared with 72 on August 3.
JPML reports 72 pending actions in MDL-3171 on August 3, 2026.
The JPML created MDL-3171 before Judge Rita F. Lin, rejecting Lyft's argument that claims should proceed in the California state coordinated proceeding.
